newsitem.title: IRAQ: Chinese delegation in Baghdad to sign oil deal.
newsitem.headline: Chinese delegation in Baghdad to sign oil deal.

text.p: A Chinese oil delegation arrived in Baghdad on Sunday for discussions which may lead to the signing of a contract to develop oilfields in southern Iraq.

The delegation headed by the chairman of the Chinese National Petroleum Corporation (CNPC) Zhou Yong-Kang includes 31 members and is expected to sign an agreement covering the billion-barrel Ahdab oilfield in southern Iraq.
"We are here to conduct discussions with the Iraqi oil minister about oil cooperation between the two countries," Yong- Kang told reporters on arrival.
He gave no further details but Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said at a news conference on Friday he hoped the Ahdab contract with the Chinese would be signed soon.
Shaheen said the Chinese were also interested in the development of the prized Halfaya field also in the south.
Halfaya was discovered 20 years ago and is believed to hold commercial reserves of about five billion barrels. Iraq believes the field could produce some 250,000 barrels a day (bpd) at full capacity.

Iraq and Russia signed in March a $3.5 billion contract to develop seven to eight billion barrels of reserves in southern Iraq's Qurna oilfield, 500 km (300 miles) south of Baghdad. The deal will be implemented over 23 years.
Officials at Iraq's oil ministry said Yong-Kang was looking forward to sign a contract similar to the Iraqi-Russian one.
Implementation of such contracts cannot be carried out as long as Iraq remains under United Nations sanctions imposed for its 1990 invasion of Kuwait.
The curbs place a blanket ban both on Iraqi exports and on investment in the country. The U.N. has allowed Iraq to pump $2 billion worth of oil over six months to pay for humanitarian purchases.
Iraq said on Friday it completed its export quota under the six-month pact. The plan comes under review on June 9.
